headword: {浄土真宗|じょうどしんしゅう}

definitions.gloss: Jōdo Shinshū; True Pure Land Buddhism
definitions.explanation: The Buddhist school founded by Shinran (1173–1263), which teaches that anyone can be saved by relying on the vow of Amida Buddha. It is the largest Buddhist denomination in Japan.

examples.japanese: ⟦{実家|じっか}→実家：03076_jikka⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{浄土真宗|じょうどしんしゅう}だ。
{浄土真宗|じょうどしんしゅう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{開祖|かいそ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{親鸞|しんらん}→親鸞：33061_shinran⟧だ。
examples.english: The founder of Jōdo Shinshū is Shinran.

examples.japanese: {浄土真宗|じょうどしんしゅう}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{阿弥陀仏|あみだぶつ}→阿弥陀仏：25098_amidabutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{力|ちから}→力：01661_chikara⟧⟦によって→によって：06801_niyotte⟧⟦{誰|だれ}→誰：00534_dare⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{救|すく}われる→救う：02063_sukuu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{教|おし}える→教える：00526_oshieru⟧。
examples.english: Jōdo Shinshū teaches that anyone can be saved by the power of Amida Buddha.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
- ⟦{親鸞|しんらん}→親鸞：33061_shinran⟧ was a disciple of ⟦{法然|ほうねん}→法然：31900_hounen⟧, founder of the ⟦{浄土宗|じょうどしゅう}→浄土宗：31849_joudoshuu⟧; the head temples are the two {本願寺|ほんがんじ} in Kyoto (Nishi and Higashi)
- It stresses reliance on Amida's power (⟦{他力|たりき}→他力：08514_tariki⟧) rather than one's own efforts; the ⟦{念仏|ねんぶつ}→念仏：12850_nenbutsu⟧ {南無阿弥陀仏|なむあみだぶつ} is said in gratitude
- Its priests have long been allowed to marry, unlike those of most older schools

USAGE:
- Often shortened to {真宗|しんしゅう}; history books also call it {一向宗|いっこうしゅう}
